text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The first Tudor King of England, HENRY VII, was born on this day in 1457.
HENRY MORTON STANLEY, the Welsh explorer who went to Africa in 1868 to find the missing DR LIVINGSTONE, was born in 1841.
Canadian engineer GEORGE CHAFFEY, who developed irrigation at Mildura and Renmark, was born in 1848.
Australian engineer LOUIS BRENNAN was born in 1852. He developed the prototype monorail, but Authorities decided two rails were better than one.
Welsh geologist Sir TANNANT EDGEWORTH DAVID, the first man to climb Mount Erebus in Antarctica, was born on this day in 1858.

British pop/jazz clarinetist and composer ACKER BILK was born in 1929. After learning to play the clarinet during army service he formed his own group in 1958. His hits included "Summer Set" (1960), "Buona Sera" (1960), "That's My Home" (1961) and "Stranger On The Shore" (1961).
American actor, writer and director ALAN ALDA was born in 1936.

Australian feminist author GERMAINE GREER was born in 1939. She gained international recognition with her book "The Female Eunuch" in 1970. Later works included "The Obstacle Race" in 1979, which was a study of contemporary women artists and "Sex and Destiny: The Politics of Human Fertility" in 1984.
** EVENTS **
1547 : King HENRY VIII of England died in London after a
38-year reign.
1807 : London became the first city in the world to be
lit by gaslight.
1855 : The Panama Railway was completed, linking the
Atlantic and the Pacific Oceans.
1896 : English motorist WALTER ARNOLD of Kent became the
first person ever to be convicted of speeding. He was doing 8 miles an hour in a 2 mile an hour area, and was chased and overtaken by a Policeman on a bicycle. He was fined one Shilling.
1911 : The Hope Diamond, which had a history of bad luck,
and was once worn by MARIE ANTIONETTE, was sold for $300,000.
1935 : Iceland became the first country to make abortion
a legal operation.
1939 : German chemist and Nobel prizewinner OTTO HAHN
revealed he'd discovered how to split the atom, unleashing enormous power.
1953 : 19 year-old DEREK BENTLEY was hanged in London,
after being convicted of murdering a policeman.
1956 : ELVIS PRESLEY made his first television
appearance.
1963 : Actress MARCIA HATHAWAY was fatally mauled by a
shark at Sydney's Balmoral beach.
1966 : The three Beaumont children went missing near the

South Australian seaside suburb of Glenelg. The children's disappearance is still one of Australia's major unsolved mysteries. JANE, nine, her seven-year-old sister ANNA and four-year-old GRANT were last seen late morning after catching a bus from nearby Somerton. Police and family members mounted a huge search for the three children. The children were never found.
1978 : Rock guitarist TED NUGENT caused a storm of
criticism by carving his autograph on a fan's arm, using the point of a knife.
1982: Italian troops stormed an apartment in Padua,
freeing kidnapped US Brigadier-General JAMES DOZIER, who'd been held by terrorists for 42 days.
1986 : The American Space Shuttle CHALLENGER exploded in
a ball of fire, killing all seven astronauts aboard, including High School teacher CHRISTA McAULIFFE.
1988 : An appeal by six Irishmen convicted of the
Birmingham pub bombing in 1975 was rejected at the Old Bailey. They became known as the "Birmingham Six".
